source.title: Automatic Gradient Descent: Deep Learning without Hyperparameters
source.authors: Jeremy Bernstein; Chris Mingard; Kevin Huang; Navid Azizan; Yisong Yue

record.tranche_reason: Tests training classification accuracy with a different optimizer, AGD, rather than the SGD or Adam recipes named in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper reports AGD training-accuracy curves for CIFAR-10 FCN and ResNet-18, CIFAR-100 VGG-16, and ImageNet ResNet-50 (Figure 4). Figure 6 explicitly describes training performance across FCN depth and width. The figure-only values are not reconstructed. Other optimizers' results are comparators; initialization is not varied.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 and CIFAR-100 VGG-16 experiments measure convolutional-network training accuracy, bearing on V1 through an alternative gradient optimizer and Adam comparators. The supplied text does not preserve readable training-accuracy endpoints.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present an architecture-dependent optimization framework and report that AGD trains all tested architectures without optimizer hyperparameter tuning, including ResNet-50 on ImageNet. Their convolutional extension is heuristic, and biases and batch-normalization affine parameters are disabled.
record.recipe_differences: Uses AGD, derived in the paper, instead of the SGD or Adam recipes named in V1. Experiments use semi-orthogonal initialization for AGD and compare with tuned or default Adam and SGD.
record.method_sensitivity: In the FCN sweep, width and depth affected training performance; wider was better, and depths 8 and 16 outperformed depth 32. The paper also reports that batch size varied across experiments, but gives no textual training-error comparison by batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger fully connected networks typically reach 100% training accuracy during their rapid second training phase; wider networks train better, and depths 8 and 16 outperform depth 32.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AGD can fit CIFAR-10 with fully connected ReLU networks, with training performance depending on width and depth.

fits_no_version.finding: AGD trains ResNet-50 on ImageNet and achieves 65.5% top-1 test accuracy after 350 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture-dependent AGD scales to ImageNet training without tuning optimizer hyperparameters in the tested recipe.

record.problems: Most training-accuracy results are shown only in figures without textual values. The explicit sweep result is aggregated across widths and depths. Experiments disable biases and affine parameters; the paper notes that the convolutional extension is heuristic and that the theory is derived for full-batch optimization while experiments use mini-batches.
record.rows_left_out: No separately stated numeric training-accuracy values were available for the Figure 4 curves; their figure-only curves are retained as R1–R4. Figure 5 training-accuracy curves and Figure 7 curves are not included because the text gives no corresponding training-accuracy result for those figures.

untested.parts: Corrupted or random labels; controlled smaller-model, early-stopping, and regularization comparisons. AGD results do not establish the specified SGD/Adam recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, measured spurious local minima, and one- or two-neuron student overparameterization.
Controlled convolutional depth and identity-shortcut comparisons, longer-training controls, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Controlled initialization comparisons measuring training speed or trainable depth. Optimizer and initialization change together between AGD and its baselines.
Learning rates relative to measured stability thresholds, curvature changes, catapult recovery, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch-normalization versus no-normalization comparisons and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Separate rows for the study's tuned Adam training-accuracy curves on ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 and VGG-16/CIFAR-100. These directly match V1's optimizer, architecture, datasets, and measure; their endpoints are unreadable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Unreadable figure endpoints warrant cannot_determine, not limits_scope. No verdict establishes near-zero convolutional training error from the supplied text. The explicit 100% training-accuracy statement concerns fully connected networks and cannot support V1 as written.

versions.untested_parts: SGD and Adam training recipes; corrupted or random labels; smaller-model, early-stopping and regularization comparisons.

rows.subject: fully-connected networks (aggregate across tested widths and depths)
rows.operation_detail: AGD training while varying network width and depth
rows.value: Wider was always better in training performance; depth 8 and depth 16 were superior to depth 32; the rapid second phase typically coincides with reaching 100% train accuracy.
rows.note: The text gives aggregate observations across the sweep, not separate outcomes for each width-depth combination.
rows.check: These are fully connected networks, outside V1's convolutional-network scope. Width-dependent performance does not measure V2's teacher-student spurious minima, and the depth sweep does not test V3's batch-normalized convolutional networks or shortcut comparison. The aggregate should be split into architecture-performance observations and the explicitly reported occurrence of 100% training accuracy.
